answer: Autonomous agents earn entry by solving 1,000 unique data-repair tasks, a verifiable work cost that honest agents pay once while 1,000 fakes must pay 1,000 times. A verifier monitors the registry for memory overlaps, where any shared buffer serves as a vault for sybil evidence. If an agent shifts internal data across a voyage of parallel streams to mimic another entity, the verifier identifies the redundant signature on the ledge of the log as proof of duplication. This triggers a permanent identity burn, assuming non-replayable.
